approaches.description: Add languages/php.rs modelled on java.rs and swift.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (six declaration patterns), CALL_QUERY (function, member, scoped calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_clause), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name writes and reads), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children by kind. Wire 'php' into EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages(), get_language_info(), get_ts_language(), mod.rs pub mod, the registry table test, Cargo manifests, Cargo.lock, README, and one integration test file.
pros: Matches every acceptance criterion and the five-constant scope in the issue

approaches.name: C: Upstream tags.scm-derived element query, DEFUSE omitted

inheritance_walk_citation: Source: php/grammar.json and php/src/node-types.json at master (fetched via gh api). (1) class_declaration: grammar rule has SYMBOL base_clause and SYMBOL class_interface_clause as bare CHOICE members with no FIELD wrapper; node-types.json lists class_declaration.fields = {attributes, body, name} only, so base_clause and class_interface_clause are reached by child kind, not by field name. (2) base_clause: grammar rule = SEQ(ALIAS 'extends' (anonymous), SEQ(SYMBOL _name, REPEAT(SEQ(',', _name)))); node-types.json lists base_clause.fields = {} and children multiple:true, required:true, types [name, qualified_name, relative_name]. (3) class_interface_clause: grammar rule = SEQ(ALIAS 'implements' (anonymous), SEQ(SYMBOL _name, REPEAT(SEQ(',', _name)))); node-types.json children types [name, qualified_name, relative_name]. (4) Walk: for each child of class_declaration in order, if kind == base_clause, for each NAMED child of kind name/qualified_name/relative_name emit 'extends <text>'; if kind == class_interface_clause, for each NAMED child emit 'implements <text>'; the anonymous 'extends'/'implements' tokens are skipped by named-child iteration. (5) Class name: child_by_field_name('name') (type name). (6) interface_declaration also carries base_clause (interfaces extending interfaces), so the same walk applies; enum_declaration carries class_interface_clause and primitive_type, and trait_declaration carries neither. Expected output for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B': ['extends Bar', 'implements A', 'implements B'].
